claims.claim: BLR main text literally states that a field k of prime characteristic p has only trivial idempotents in kG when all finite subgroups of G are p-groups, without adding soficity to the field branch.
claims.limit: This records the published assertion, not an independent proof or truth validation.

claims.claim: The cited Formanek/Burger-Valette chain verifies prime-characteristic conjugacy-class trace vanishing and tau(e) in {0,1}, but the inspected primary sources use a characteristic-zero detector for e=0 or 1.
claims.source: Formanek 1973 pp.366-369; Burger-Valette 1998 pp.225-227; BLR companion lines 975-986
claims.limit: A gap in the advertised route is not a counterexample to the BLR assertion; another proof could exist.

claims.claim: If char(k)=p and G is residually a finite p-group, then kG has no nontrivial idempotents.
claims.proof: Finite support is separated injectively in one finite p-group quotient; the image of a zero-augmentation idempotent lies in the nilpotent augmentation ideal of kP.
claims.limit: This does not cover the supplied N129 group if its nonzero c dies in every finite quotient.

claims.claim: The residual-p detector cannot apply to N129 if the source card's finite-quotient-killing property for c is valid.
claims.limit: The N129 witness and graph remain conditional and unacquired.

claims.claim: Two explicit finite planar band diagrams over an immersed K4 verify the local distinct-disk and self-paired same-edge surgery with a fixed nonempty outer word.
claims.limit: The K4 is not claimed to satisfy the full bounded closed-system exclusion; no N129 source graph or random graph was acquired.

claims.claim: The literal BLR unconditional field-of-prime-characteristic idempotent assertion versus the conditional N129 witness remains unresolved.
claims.limit: No explicit counterexample to an actually established group-algebra lemma was found; N129 remains conditional.
